subject: Mathematics
unit: Summer 1: Geometric notation and constructions; geometric reasoning
source: Seeded from mathematics/y7 lesson 59 (Printable construction sheet: bisectors (portal worksheet for this lesson))
intro: Lesson 59: Constructing the perpendicular bisector of a line segment. To understand how to construct a perpendicular bisector with compasses and why it works

model.title: Construct the perpendicular bisector of AB = 8 cm.

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: Open the compasses to more than half of AB, for example 5 cm

parts.label: Step 2
parts.text: Draw arcs above and below the line from A

parts.label: Step 3
parts.text: Keep the radius: arcs above and below from B

parts.label: Step 4
parts.text: Join the two crossing points with a ruler

parts.label: Answer
parts.text: It crosses AB at the midpoint, 4 cm from each end, at 90°

questions.q: Construct the perpendicular bisector of a 6 cm line. Measure each half and the angle.
questions.model: Compasses at about 4 cm; arcs from both ends above and below; join the crossings. Measure 3 cm and 3 cm and check 90° with a protractor.

questions.q: Point P is on the perpendicular bisector of CD and PC = 7 cm. Find PD.

(a) Draw AB = 10 cm and construct its perpendicular bisector. (b) Mark the midpoint M and measure AM. (c) Mark any point P on the bisector; measure PA and PB. (d) Draw any triangle and construct the perpendicular bisectors of two of its sides.
questions.a: (a) arcs visible (b) AM = 5 cm (c) PA = PB (d) the bisectors cross at a point the same distance from all three vertices
questions.model: (a) Compasses at 6 cm. Arcs from A and from B, above and below; join the two crossings with a ruler.

questions.q: Two villages A and B are 6 km apart (1 cm = 1 km). A well must be the same distance from both and 5 km from A. Construct its possible positions.
questions.a: Construct the perpendicular bisector of AB; an arc of 5 cm from A cuts it in two places, each 4 km from the midpoint.

questions.q: Explain why the three perpendicular bisectors of a triangle meet at one point.
questions.a: Where two meet, the point is equidistant from all three vertices, so it must also lie on the third bisector.

questions.q: The perpendicular bisector of AB crosses AB at:
Q is on the perpendicular bisector of EF and QE = 4.5 cm. Find QF.
Big question: how can you find the exact middle of a line without measuring?
questions.a: Construct the perpendicular bisector with equal arcs from both ends: it crosses at the midpoint.
